rows.description: I scored the most and feel like showing off. Being glad is fine; a good winner shares joy modestly and remembers that friends who scored less still have strengths.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: disillusionment, envy, fear, shame

rows.description: I got fewer marks than I hoped and think I am stupid. One result is not a verdict on me; a wiser view asks which topics went wrong and how to practise them.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: disillusionment, envy, fear, pride

rows.description: My teacher says she sees my effort even though my marks are low. I feel seen. I learn that effort counts and that one person's belief can steady me on a bad day.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: disillusionment, envy, fear, pride, shame
possibly related concept (heuristic): Locus of control

rows.description: A friend says, just show me your answers, we are friends after all. I feel pulled between loyalty and honesty. A real friend won't make me risk trouble; I can say no and offer to help him study.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: coercion, contempt, fear, guilt, indebtedness, temptation

rows.description: I know the answer is in my friend's paper and nobody is looking. Part of me wants the marks, part of me wants to be proud of myself. Choosing honesty builds a strength that marks cannot.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: coercion, contempt, fear, guilt, indebtedness, manipulation

rows.description: I copied once and got away with it, but I feel uneasy. That unease is a sign of my conscience. Admitting it or deciding not to repeat it is better than pretending nothing happened.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: coercion, contempt, fear, indebtedness, manipulation, temptation

rows.description: I am afraid the teacher will notice my glance at another paper. Fear of getting caught is not the same as caring about honesty, and I can ask myself what I would do if nobody ever found out.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: coercion, contempt, guilt, indebtedness, manipulation, temptation

rows.description: My parents demand the top rank, and I feel cheating is my only way out. I can tell them honestly how heavy the pressure is; a lower honest score is safer than a high dishonest one.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: contempt, fear, guilt, indebtedness, manipulation, temptation

rows.description: I feel superior to a classmate who cheats and tell everyone. Being angry at dishonesty is fair, but gossip does not help; reporting to a teacher quietly, if needed, is more mature.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: coercion, fear, guilt, indebtedness, manipulation, temptation

rows.description: My friend once helped me with homework and now expects me to help him cheat. Being grateful does not mean I must do wrong; I can repay him in honest ways.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: coercion, contempt, fear, guilt, manipulation, temptation
